title: Cirrus SR22 G5 — Emergency Procedures
description: Emergency procedures for the Cirrus SR22 G5 with Continental IO-550 fuel-injected engine and Cirrus Airframe Parachute System (CAPS). Memory items are marked. CAPS is a primary emergency tool on this aircraft — when in doubt, pull. All numeric limits, airspeeds, and CAPS deployment envelope must come from the specific aircraft POH/AFM. Not a substitute for Cirrus factory transition training or recurrent emergency training.

source.notes: No manufacturer document consulted. Written from general familiarity with the type.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities, or other limitations — must come from aircraft POH. CAPS deployment envelope (minimum altitude, airspeed) is POH-specific and is NOT contained here.
Equipment variations exist across SR22 G5 aircraft. Verify all emergency procedures against the specific aircraft POH before flight.

rights.notes: Manufacturer POH and AFM remain under copyright. This file does not reproduce their wording or selection of items.

items.text: Landing site — select largest, flattest field aligned with wind if possible; commit to it early
Mayday — transmit on 121.5 MHz; squawk 7700
Fuel selector
Mixture
Ignition switch
Master switch — off before touchdown to eliminate electrical ignition sources
Seat belts and shoulder harnesses — all occupants cinch tight; advise to brace
Flaps — extend for landing on confirmed reachable field; consider partial flaps if field is short
Doors — unlatch prior to touchdown to ensure exit ability after impact
Consider CAPS deployment if unable to reach a suitable landing surface and altitude allows. CAPS is the preferred outcome over an uncontrolled off-airport landing in unsurvivable terrain.

sections.title: CAPS Deployment — Cirrus Airframe Parachute System

items.text: CAPS IS A LAST-RESORT AND IN CERTAIN EMERGENCY SCENARIOS THE PREFERRED OPTION. Deploy without hesitation when the aircraft cannot be controlled, when terrain precludes a survivable landing, or when the pilot becomes incapacitated. All numeric deployment envelope limits (minimum altitude, airspeed) come from the POH — not this file.
Announce to occupants
Throttle
items.response: REDUCE AS PRACTICAL; DO NOT DELAY PULL

items.text: CAPS handle — grasp T-handle overhead; pull firmly through full stroke
items.response: PULL HARD UNTIL DETENT FELT; DO NOT STOP PARTWAY

items.text: Master switch — after chute deploys and aircraft stabilizes under canopy
Fuel selector
Mixture
Ignition switch
Seat belts and shoulder harnesses — all occupants cinched as tight as possible
Brace position — all occupants; brace against seats; hands off all controls
After landing under CAPS: exit the aircraft quickly if fire risk exists. Do not restart the engine. Emergency services will respond to ELT and/or transmitted position.
